# c3-bot relay inbox (#1795)
- Every session, local and cloud, gets the c3-bot Telegram relay inbox by default: the SessionStart hook relay-inbox.sh is declared once in the SoT (settings.project.json, hooks.json) and deployed to every repo. Why: owner messages must reach a working session without manual setup. Guard: test-claude-sot.sh, hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh.
- Mesh host (health at http://10.0.0.6:3119/c3bot-relay/health answers): the hook claims the lease, polls `GET /c3bot-relay/poll?after=<cursor>&wait=0` with the bearer from C3BOT_RELAY_TOKEN, keeps the cursor in ~/.claude/c3bot-relay-cursor and injects new routed owner messages as additionalContext; run `.claude/hooks/c3/relay-inbox.sh check` to read again later. Why: one cheap poll, no daemon. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh.
- Cloud container (relay not reachable): arm exactly ONE self re-arming 10-minute send_later check; it reads the relay through cloud-infra-mcp (devops docker_exec, vm oci-apps, container c3bot-relay, a `node -e fetch` to the mesh address 10.0.0.6:3119 with the container's own token env; the image has node, no wget or curl, and the relay does not listen on loopback), answers, and acknowledges with devops telegram_send. Never two pending checks. Why: containers are off the mesh; duplicate loops double-answer. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh (instruction text).
- The hook always exits 0, finishes in under 5 s (hard timeout) and prints nothing when there is nothing new, no token, or the relay is down off a cloud container. Why: a SessionStart hook must never block or spam a session. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh.
- The token is never printed, never put on a command line or in a URL; curl gets it on stdin (-K -), the container path uses the container's own env. Why: rules/security.md. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh checks argv and output.
- Exactly one session answers each owner message. A reply (reply_to_message.message_id) goes to the session that sent the original: matched by the session's sent log or by the tag in the original text. A non-reply message goes only to the current holder of the relay lease. Why: several sessions read the same inbox. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh (one winner, reply routing).
- Every send through the c3-bot starts with the session tag `[c3:xxxxxx]` (first 6 characters of the session id; `relay-inbox.sh tag` prints it), and the session logs each returned message_id with `relay-inbox.sh sent <message_id>` (~/.claude/c3bot-relay-sent.log). The tag in the text is the cross-host route; the log is the same-host route. The hook also fills the log from relay telegram.sent events ({text, message_ids}) whose text starts with the tag, and reads the reply target from the raw update (update.message or update.edited_message .reply_to_message). Why: reply routing depends on it. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh.
- Lease: `POST /c3bot-relay/claim {session, ttl}` is a TTL lease; the first claimer wins, the holder renews by claiming again, and the lease expires after ttl seconds so another session can take it. The hook claims with ttl 900 (C3BOT_LEASE_TTL). Why: a dead holder must not hold the inbox forever. Guard: relay test in cloudy-u-containers infra-ops_c3bot-relay.
- Sessions on one host share the cursor; a message routed to another session is kept in ~/.claude/c3bot-relay-pending.jsonl (last 50) for its owner instead of being dropped. Why: the shared cursor must not swallow another session's messages. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh (shared host case).
- C3BOT_RELAY=0 disables the hook for a session. Why: an opt-out for test and beacon sessions. Guard: hooks/tests/relay-inbox.sh.
